Quantile random forest for conditional growth predictions

Source: R/quant-forest.R
wgh_quantile_forest.Rd

Fits a quantile regression forest (ranger with quantreg = TRUE) of the target z-score on the baseline features, separately by sex and target age, and predicts any quantile for new children. It is a flexible, assumption-light benchmark for the linear conditional references of wgh_condref(): if the forest does not predict better out of sample, the simpler, interpretable model is preferred (Book 2 Chapter 15).

Usage

wgh_quantile_forest(
  panel,
  formula = ~baseline_haz + baseline_baz + baseline_age,
  taus = wgh_taus(c(0.03, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95, 0.97)),
  num.trees = 500,
  min.node.size = 5,
  min_n = 30,
  seed = 2026
)

# S3 method for class 'wgh_qrf'
predict(object, newdata, ...)

Arguments

panel

Output of wgh_conditional_panel().

formula

Right-hand side with the baseline features.

taus

Quantiles to predict.

num.trees, min.node.size

Forest settings passed to ranger::ranger().

min_n

Smallest number of children needed to fit a cell.

seed

Random seed of the forests.

object

A wgh_qrf object.

newdata

Rows with sex, target_nominal and the baseline features.

...

Unused.

Value

An object of class wgh_qrf with one forest per sex and target age. predict() returns a matrix of quantiles (one row per child, rearranged to be monotone).

Next steps

Compare the forest with the conditional reference out of sample with wgh_condref_cv() (forest = TRUE) or child by child with wgh_condref_compare().

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cp <- wgh_conditional_panel(growdat, targets = c(10, 12))
  qrf <- wgh_quantile_forest(cp, num.trees = 200)
  qrf
  round(predict(qrf, cp[1:3, ]), 2)
}
#>      q0.030 q0.050 q0.100 q0.250 q0.500 q0.750 q0.900 q0.950 q0.970
#> [1,]   0.22   0.46   0.81   1.38   2.05   2.05   2.07   2.54   2.54
#> [2,]   0.15   0.78   0.92   0.94   1.13   1.21   1.43   1.68   1.84
#> [3,]   0.33   0.34   0.52   0.88   1.16   1.19   1.51   1.77   1.77
# }
